summary_for_children: Al-'Ankabut means The Spider. It teaches that faith is tested, and that relying on anything besides Allah is like the spider's home, the weakest of homes. It mentions Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut and others.
environment_concept: A huge, fine spider's web (29:41), a road through many landscapes (29:20) and an ark resting on a ridge as a sign (29:15).
architecture_and_scenery: Rock and timber houses, a vast dew-covered web between trees, an ark on a ridge, and a long road through changing lands.

palette.lighting: Morning dew catching the light on the web

areas.name: The Spider's Web
areas.description: A huge, beautiful but fragile web.

areas.name: Ark on the Ridge
areas.description: An ark resting on a ridge as a sign.

activities.name: Test the homes
activities.description: Push gently on the web and the stone house to see which stands (adaptation).
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Observe creation
activities.description: Find five glowing things along the road.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Narration uses the spider's example to talk about what truly protects us.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.
